questions.feedback: That same-pressure answer is the one to unlearn: The same push gives the same pressure whether you stand flat or on tiptoes. Reteach point: Pressure is force over area: tiptoes spread the same force over a smaller area, so the pressure is higher.
questions.misconception: The same push gives the same pressure whether you stand flat or on tiptoes.
questions.prompt: Standing on tiptoes instead of flat feet, with the same weight, what happens to the pressure under your feet?

questions.feedback: Scene s2 fixes this: moment = force x distance = 30 x 1.0 = 30 newton-metres, matching the other side.
questions.prompt: A 30 N weight balances a beam when it sits 1.0 m from the pivot. What moment does it make?

questions.feedback: Scene s3: the area falls to one tenth, so the pressure rises tenfold - 200 / 0.05 = 4000 pascals.
questions.prompt: The same 200 N crate is tipped from a 0.5 square metre face onto a 0.05 square metre edge. The pressure changes from 400 Pa to what?

questions.answer: The net force is 20 N in the direction of the push, so the block keeps sliding.
questions.feedback: Scene s1: friction opposes the slide but is smaller than the push - 60 - 40 leaves a net 20 newtons to the right.
questions.prompt: A push of 60 N meets friction of 40 N. Why does the block keep sliding instead of stopping?
